skill.name: policy-opa
skill.description: Create, test, and integrate Open Policy Agent policies for Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, and compliance workflows.
skill.summary: Build and validate OPA Rego policies for security, compliance, Kubernetes admission control, and CI/CD enforcement.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate OPA policy-as-code guide with many static false positives caused by Markdown code blocks, Rego keywords, and examples that intentionally detect insecure infrastructure patterns. Confirmed residual risks are limited to unpinned external download or apply commands and CI examples that evaluate Terraform plan JSON, which can contain sensitive values if users print or archive outputs carelessly.

remediation.issue: Unpinned remote install and deployment examples
remediation.suggestion: Pin OPA and Gatekeeper versions, prefer official setup actions, and document checksum or signature verification for downloaded binaries and manifests.

remediation.issue: Terraform plan JSON may include sensitive values
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to print full plan-derived outputs in CI logs and to redact or restrict artifacts created from Terraform plan evaluation.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples rely on local shell and cluster commands
remediation.suggestion: State that commands should be run only in authorized repositories, clusters, and CI environments with least-privilege credentials.

content.value_statement: Security teams need repeatable policy checks across clusters, infrastructure, and compliance controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through OPA Rego policy creation, testing, and CI/CD enforcement.
actual_capabilities: Explains OPA and Rego workflows for security and compliance policy enforcement.
Provides Kubernetes admission control policy patterns and Gatekeeper examples.
Shows Terraform and infrastructure-as-code validation patterns for pre-deployment checks.
Maps policies to compliance frameworks such as SOC2, PCI-DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, NIST, and ISO27001.
Includes CI/CD examples for testing policies and failing builds on violations.
Covers troubleshooting, monitoring, reporting, and performance guidance for OPA deployments.
limitations: It does not prove that generated policies satisfy legal or auditor requirements.
It assumes users have authorized access to the target repository, cluster, or CI system.
Some examples require external tools such as OPA, kubectl, Terraform, jq, or yq.
Remote install examples should be pinned and verified before production use.

use_cases.title: Kubernetes admission control
use_cases.description: Create Rego policies and Gatekeeper constraints that block privileged pods, missing labels, or unsafe runtime settings.

use_cases.title: Infrastructure policy validation
use_cases.description: Check Terraform or CloudFormation changes before deployment and fail CI when insecure network, storage, or IAM patterns appear.

use_cases.title: Compliance control automation
use_cases.description: Map SOC2, PCI-DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, NIST, or ISO27001 controls into testable OPA policies and reports.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the policy-opa skill to write a simple Rego policy that denies Kubernetes pods running as privileged containers.

prompt_templates.title: Test an existing policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the policy-opa skill to create unit tests for this Rego policy and explain what each test proves.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI policy validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the policy-opa skill to design a CI workflow that tests OPA policies and blocks deployment when violations exist.

prompt_templates.title: Map controls to policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the policy-opa skill to map these compliance requirements to OPA policies, tests, and audit report outputs.

output_examples.input: Ask for a Kubernetes pod security policy.
output_examples.output: A Rego policy outline that denies privileged containers, requires non-root execution, and explains the matching Gatekeeper deployment steps.

output_examples.input: Ask for Terraform policy validation in CI.
output: Guidance for creating Terraform plan JSON safely.
Recommendations for redacting sensitive CI output.

output_examples.output: A control-to-policy plan that connects each requirement to Rego rules, tests, evidence collection, and audit reporting.

best_practices: Run policy checks in least-privilege CI and cluster contexts.
Write unit tests for every policy rule before enforcement.
Pin external tool and manifest versions before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets or full Terraform plan outputs into prompts or public logs.
Do not apply remote Kubernetes manifests without version pinning and review.
Do not treat generated policy text as auditor-approved evidence without validation.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps create, test, and operate Open Policy Agent policies for security, compliance, Kubernetes, and infrastructure workflows.

faq.question: Does it execute OPA commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance. Users choose which commands to run in their own authorized environment.

faq.question: Can it create Kubernetes admission policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Rego and Gatekeeper patterns for enforcing pod and workload security requirements.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps policy examples to frameworks such as SOC2, PCI-DSS, GDPR, HIPAA, NIST, and ISO27001.

faq.question: What tools are usually required?
faq.answer: Common workflows use OPA, kubectl, Terraform, jq, yq, and CI/CD runners.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review generated policies, test coverage, CI permissions, external downloads, and any logs that may include sensitive plan data.
